advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-point the LLMConfig per cell using `cell.config_file` (or assert/skip when the resolved provider != `cell.provider`) so a multi-credential run cannot mislabel scores.
evidence: tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py:172: `config = LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=str(rebar_repo))` (inside `for cell in cells:` but not keyed on `cell.config_file`)
`search_files` for `config_file` in the harness returns no matches — `cell.config_file` is never read

Comment at line 170-171 claims each cell 'is selected through its committed overlay ... dogfoods the same REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE override path', but the loop does not set REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE per cell
all_scores key/label `f"{cell.provider}__{variant}"` (line 185) attributes replies to cell.provider regardless of the provider actually called
advisory.finding: The live harness never applies `cell.config_file`; it derives `config` once from the ambient `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` and reuses it for every measured cell, so a run with more than one provider credential present calls the single REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE-selected provider for all cells while labelling each with its (wrong) `cell.provider`.
scenarios: An operator runs the harness locally (or any environment) with two or more provider credentials present: every measured cell issues calls against the one provider REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE points at, but the score table labels them anthropic/bedrock/openai — silently wrong before/after numbers.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a classify_layout golden that forces a precedence decision (e.g. a reply with two DISTINCT objects that are ALSO both fenced) asserting 'multi_object' wins over 'fenced'.
evidence: _structured_matrix.py:157-167 evaluates precedence: `if len(distinct) >= 2: return "multi_object"` then `if _has_fenced_json(text): return "fenced"` then inline-quoted → "quoted_json"

_LAYOUT_GOLDENS at tests/unit/test_structured_matrix_scorer.py:57-62 maps one clean fixture per class; no fixture combines classes (e.g. two objects that are ALSO both fenced, exercising multi_object-over-fenced)
layout_fenced.json contains exactly one fenced object and layout_multi_object.json two bare objects — neither forces a precedence decision between the branches
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `classify_layout` in tests returns only the single golden-loop assertion at line 103; no mixed-precedence case exists
_structured_matrix.py:104-111 `_distinct_values` does a linear equality dedup; classify_layout at line 158-160 keys `multi_object` off `len(distinct) >= 2`
_structured_matrix.py:151-152 docstring: 'deduped by equal Python value, so the same object is never double-counted'

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `_distinct_values` in tests returns no test reference; the only multi_object golden (layout_multi_object.json:5) contains two DISTINCT objects, so the dedup branch never fires with equal duplicates
_structured_matrix.py:156 docstring: 'prose — otherwise (a single bare object mid-prose, OR NO parseable object at all)'
layout_prose.json:5 reply embeds a valid `{"verdict": "PASS", ...}` object — it exercises the single-bare-object path, not the no-object path

_structured_matrix.py:161-167: when `len(distinct) == 0` the branch is skipped and control falls through to `return "prose"` — this fall-through is only reached with distinct==1 in the current goldens
advisory.finding: classify_layout's documented precedence ordering (multi_object > fenced > quoted_json) is never tested on a mixed-class input; every layout golden is a clean single-class example, so a precedence-inversion mutant (e.g. returning 'fenced' for a fenced multi-object, or 'quoted_json' before checking fenced) passes all committed tests.
merged_from: The _distinct_values dedup ('the same object is never double-counted', so two identical top-level objects must NOT classify as multi_object) is untested; a broken-dedup mutant that counts by raw span instead of distinct value would still pass every committed golden.

The 'prose' fallback branch for a reply with NO parseable JSON object at all is untested; the only prose golden contains a single bare parseable object, so the empty/no-object arm of classify_layout has no coverage.
scenarios: A refactor reorders the precedence checks (e.g. checks fenced before object count) and a fenced multi-object reply is misclassified, silently skewing the layout-rate table the sentinel sibling reasons over

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Install the provider SDKs the matrix arms need — use `--extra dev` (or add `--extra bedrock`/openai) so the bedrock (boto3) and openai arms can make live calls, instead of `--extra agents` which omits them.
evidence: structured-output-baseline.yml:71  `          uv sync --locked --extra agents`
pyproject.toml:138-140 `pulling in boto3 for every install would defeat the lean default. ... kept OUT of the` and pyproject.toml:142 `bedrock = [` (a separate extra, not in `agents`)

pyproject.toml:245-247 `# Bedrock provider support ... Opt-in at runtime (kept OUT of the` / `# agents extra — pip install nava-rebar[agents] must still install without boto3)` and line 244 `"pydantic-ai-slim[openai]>=1,<2",` — both live only in `dev`
external-integration.yml:171-176 sibling uses `uv sync --locked --extra dev` with comment `[dev] already pulls pydantic-ai-slim's [bedrock] and [openai] groups, so one sync covers every arm`
tests/external/_live_llm.py:78-81 bedrock credential probe returns False when boto3 is absent (`except ImportError: return False`)

structured-output-baseline.yml steps list has no 'Require this arm's credential' preflight — the run step at line 80 goes straight to `pytest ...` (ABSENCE: no `exit 1`/`::error` preflight step in the file)
external-integration.yml:55-63 `AN ARM WITH NO CREDENTIAL FAILS; IT DOES NOT SKIP. ... a skipped job renders grey/neutral, which is trivially misread as fine`
external-integration.yml:115-154 the 'Require this arm's credential (loud failure, never a silent skip)' step with `exit 1` + `::error`
tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:341-357 `test_the_credential_preflight_fails_loudly_for_every_arm` enforces that preflight for the sibling workflow
tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py:157-160 the harness `pytest.skip(...)` when no cell is measured
advisory.finding: The workflow installs only `uv sync --locked --extra agents`, but the `agents` extra deliberately excludes boto3 and the bedrock/openai provider SDKs, so the bedrock and openai matrix arms of this billable workflow cannot make live calls (bedrock: no boto3 -> credential probe silently returns 'unmeasured'; openai: OPENAI_API_KEY passes the readiness gate but the openai SDK is absent -> model construction fails).
merged_from: The workflow has no loud credential preflight step; an arm whose credential is absent is only handled by the harness's pytest.skip, deviating from the sibling workflow's deliberate 'an absent credential FAILS, it does not skip' design that a unit test enforces.
scenarios: An operator dispatches the workflow with all secrets present; the bedrock arm records every cell 'unmeasured' and the openai arm errors at model construction, so a paid sweep measures only anthropic while appearing configured for three providers.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the install step to `uv sync --locked --extra dev` (matching external-integration.yml), or explicitly add the needed provider extras so boto3 + pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock,openai] are installed for the bedrock/openai arms.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN/BEDROCK_REGION on `matrix.provider == 'bedrock'` on the run step, matching the region-variable guards on the same step.
evidence: structured-output-baseline.yml:89-90 `BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN: ${{ vars.AWS_BEDROCK_CI_ROLE_ARN }}` / `BEDROCK_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_BEDROCK_CI_REGION }}` — no `matrix.provider` guard
structured-output-baseline.yml:93-94 same step guards `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: ${{ matrix.provider == 'bedrock' && vars.AWS_BEDROCK_CI_REGION || '' }}` and `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` on the arm
advisory.finding: On the harness run step, BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN and BEDROCK_REGION are exported unconditionally to every matrix arm, whereas AWS_DEFAULT_REGION/REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION on the same step are correctly guarded on `matrix.provider == 'bedrock'` — an inconsistency with the file's own per-arm scoping discipline.
scenarios: The anthropic and openai arms receive the Bedrock role ARN/region env even though they never use them.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap both with the same guard, e.g. `BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN: ${{ matrix.provider == 'bedrock' && vars.AWS_BEDROCK_CI_ROLE_ARN || '' }}`.
